tasks.short: Run tests on the line or cable, read the trace to locate the fault, check the results, record them on the work order, compare the fault with network records, and report the fault location to the planner.

steps.what: Line technician inspects and tests lines or cables with the test set
Line technician measures events and the distance to the fault on the test trace
Line technician analyzes test results to assess transmission characteristics and locate faults
Line technician checks the test results before recording them
Line technician records the test results on the paper work order
Line technician compares the fault location with network records
Line technician reports the fault location to the planner by phone

tasks.design: The test set's software marks events and distance to the fault on the trace, and once the technician has checked the results they upload to the mobile work order ({OPS_SYSTEM}) instead of being written down. The network map on the tablet shows splice points and duct routes at that distance, and the fault location goes to the planner in the work order. Testing and judging the trace stay with the technician; work order times are not used to rate technicians.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were written on paper work orders and fault distances matched to paper maps.
tasks.enabler_now: Fibre test sets upload results; mobile work orders show network maps.
tasks.still_hard: Network records often differ from what is in the ground.
tasks.human_edge: Reading an odd trace as a crushed duct, not a bad splice.

evidence.claim: At Altitude Infra, a French fibre network with 500 technicians, Praxedo mobile work orders saved about 8 hours per technician per week on work-order mail, entry and reports; vendor case.
Work orders with time stamps or locations can observe technicians, so the works council must consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the fault ticket to the fault reported; the repair is outside.
Input contract: network records from the network operator; test sets with upload; fallback is paper and phone.
Testing and reading traces do not change.
Tablets have coverage or sync later.
research_questions: Do repair crews find the fault at the first dig more often?

incremental.description: Line technician reports wrong network records.

approvals.approved_version: The test results as checked by the technician in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: copper lines with older test sets; high: fibre with uploading test sets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure cable length and signal level at the tap, compute impedance and the extra resistance needed, select and fit the attenuator, and record the values on the work order.

steps.what: Line technician measures cable length and signal level from the pole to the house
Line technician computes impedance of wires and the additional resistance needed with tables
Line technician selects and fits the attenuator to reach the desired signal level
Line technician records signal values and the attenuator on the work order

tasks.design: The signal meter's app computes cable loss from cable type and length and proposes the attenuator value, so tables are not consulted. The technician enters the readings and fitted part in the mobile work order ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with pick lists. Measuring and fitting stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Losses were computed from printed tables and values written on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Signal meter apps compute cable loss from type and length.
tasks.still_hard: Old or damaged drops do not follow the tables.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a corroded connector behind a low reading.

reach.learn: Whether recorded levels show weak network sections.

evidence.claim: Signal meter apps can compute cable loss from cable type and length.

assumptions: Boundary: from the drop installation to the signal record; network amplifier settings are outside.
Input contract: cable types set by the network operator; fallback is printed tables.
Measuring and fitting do not change.
research_questions: Do repeat visits for signal problems fall?

incremental.description: Line technician checks the app's cable type before computing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly fibre drops with little attenuation work; high: mostly coax drops.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain the service and equipment to the subscriber, help set up the Wi-Fi and devices, confirm the installation is complete, give the subscriber the guides, and collect any installation fee.

steps.what: Line technician explains cable service to subscribers after installation
Line technician helps set up the Wi-Fi and devices
Line technician confirms the installation is complete and checks the guide message: the guides for the installed service and the subscriber's e-mail address
Line technician gives the subscriber the user guides; after the check in s3 the work order sends them as the guide message by e-mail
Line technician collects installation fees and writes a receipt

tasks.design: Once the technician confirms the installation and checks the guide message in the mobile work order ({OPS_SYSTEM}), the work order sends that message with the user guides and how-to videos to the subscriber's e-mail address, instead of the technician handing over a printed pack. The installation fee goes on the subscriber's first bill in the billing system ({CRM}), so the technician no longer collects money at the door. Explaining the service and setting up devices stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guides were printed and fees collected at the door with handwritten receipts.
tasks.enabler_now: Work order completion can trigger welcome messages; billing systems add one-off fees.
tasks.still_hard: Some subscribers want the technician to show every device.
tasks.human_edge: Showing an older subscriber how to call their grandchildren on the TV.

reach.learn: Whether welcome messages cut first-week calls.

evidence.claim: Work order completion can trigger customer messages; billing systems can add one-off installation fees.

assumptions: Boundary: from the installation done to the fee collected; ongoing billing is outside.
Input contract: guides kept by customer service; fees set by the provider; fallback is printed packs and cash.
Subscribers pay the fee on their first bill in about the time paying at the door took; no added subscriber time.
Explaining and setting up do not change.
research_questions: Do first-week calls from new subscribers fall?

incremental.description: Line technician checks the subscriber's e-mail address in the work order.

approvals.approved_version: The guide message with the guides for the installed service, addressed to the subscriber's e-mail address, as checked by the technician in s3; a changed address or service needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few installations with fees; high: most installations with a fee and printed packs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The line technician keeps testing, reading traces, fitting parts and explaining service to subscribers; paper work orders, tables, printed packs and cash shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the mobile work order and network map
role.ambitious_version: A technician who fixes more faults at the first visit.
